strongest_angle: NASA's Voyager 1 successfully extended its mission lifespan by optimizing power consumption, even as it continues to navigate unexpected communication gaps at extreme distances from Earth.

key_facts.fact: In September 2026, NASA engineers successfully turned off three power-hungry devices on Voyager 1 and replaced them with lower-power alternatives to extend the spacecraft's operational life.
On October 18 and 19, 2026, the Deep Space Network failed to detect radio signals from Voyager 1 during two scheduled communication attempts.
Voyager 1's communication link with Earth autonomously restored itself on October 20, 2026, after a 48-hour period of silence.
During the October 2026 communication dropout, Voyager 1 was located 16 billion miles (24 billion kilometers) away from Earth.
